Anna K.: Heads-up — after last night's Dedicated deploy the KV prefill job caused a noticeable P95 latency bump for small inference requests (~300ms -> ~520ms) and a spike in GPU memory pressure on pool-a.
Jay P.: saw the alerts. linking perf dashboard: https://redwood/dashboards/prefill-1867 :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Maria S.: What did the prefill job actually push? full prefixes or sampled set?
Anna K.: full set for the top 500 prefixes (we used the new heuristic that includes near-duplicates). The job was aggressive — launched 50 concurrent workers across nodes.
Liam W.: logs show KV writes + eviction churn: "kv_set_latency_ms p95=45 p99=210" and eviction_rate jumped from 0.8% -> 7.3% during the run.
ops-bot: Autoscaler triggered +2 nodes at 02:14 UTC because of sustained GPU memory >85%.
Jay P.: Hypothesis: our prefill keying is too granular, causing high KV set volume and thrashing the cache. Also the warmer used the heavy kernel path leading to larger KV footprints.
Maria S.: Also noticed we used non-normalized prompts — casing/extra whitespace created duplicate keys. We should normalize keys before seeding.
Anna K.: Agreed. Proposed mitigation in short term:
- Pause scheduled prefill immediately for Dedicated pool-a
- Reduce concurrency to 4 workers per node
- Switch to canonical keying (lowercase + strip whitespace)
- Only prefill top-100 prefixes per model
Jay P.: I'll pause the job now. `kubectl scale job/prefill-job -n infra --replicas=0` (done) :white_check_mark:
Liam W.: Creating a small experiment for warmers: synthetic traffic that reuses exact keys to measure hit-rate without KV churn. If we can reproduce high hit-rate with low set volume, great.
Maria S.: For longer term, here's a draft policy we can try:
1) Key normalization + fingerprinting (sha256 of normalized prompt)
2) Bloom filter in front of KV to avoid re-sets for already-present keys
3) Prefill only cold-start heavy routes (based on route telemetry)
4) Staggered scheduling: exponential backoff per node to avoid synchronized writes
Anna K.: On kernel selection side: runtime currently picks the large-kernel for these long prompts; but prefill traffic is short (prefixes). We can force the small-kernel during prefill to reduce memory per request.
Jay P.: Can we pin kernel via env override? `REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=small` for prefill pods?
Liam W.: Yes, we can. I'll bake an image with the override and run a canary prefill with reduced kernel size and 2x lower batch size.
Maria S.: Metrics to track for the canary:
- prefill write volume (writes/sec)
- kv_set_latency_ms p50/p95/p99
- cache_hit_rate per-model
- host GPU memory and eviction_rate
- end-to-end small-request p95 latency
Anna K.: Also add a metric for "prefill-induced evictions" by tagging writes from the job so we can correlate.
ops-bot: deploy-bot started job prefill-canary-186700 with env override
deploy-bot: canary image pushed: gcr.io/redwood/prefill:canary-kernel-small
Jay P.: Canary results (first 30m): write volume down 56%, eviction_rate down to 1.2%, small-request p95 restored to baseline. Cache hit-rate for seeded keys ~78% after 15m.
Maria S.: Good signal. Remaining concerns: bloom filter false positives could prevent needed writes. Need to pick acceptable FP rate (e.g., 0.1%).
Liam W.: Implementation notes:
- Use a per-model cuckoo filter backend in front of KV (memory small, low FP)
- Maintain filter persistence every 5m to avoid cold misses after restarts
- Provide a "dry-run" mode where prefill tags writes but doesn't write if bloom says present — to validate FP behavior
Anna K.: Action items:
- Jay: revert pause and rollout staggered prefill with reduced concurrency + kernel override (ETA today)
- Liam: prototype cuckoo/bloom front and dry-run mode (ETA 3d)
- Maria: add key normalization + fingerprinting utility to prefill repo and integrate (ETA 2d)
- Anna: add dashboard tiles and an alert for "prefill-eviction-rate" (ETA tomorrow)
Jay P.: I'll open PRs and post links here.
Maria S.: One more suggestion: don't prefill expired/rare prefixes — use frequency threshold from logs (e.g., > 10 hits/day) to qualify.
Liam W.: Agreed. Also consider pre-warming at deploy-time but only the model's top cold-start triggers rather than a broad sweep.
Anna K.: Thanks team. After the canary proves stable we'll roll the new policy to other pools. Let's reconvene tomorrow 10:30 UTC for a short sync.
Jay P.: PRs: https://github.com/redwood/prefill/pull/418 (concurrency+kernel), https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/222 (metric tagging)
Maria S.: I'll link the normalization PR once ready.
ops-bot: Reminder: scheduled job "prefill-nightly" remains suspended until manual resume.
Anna K.: Closing note — this is a good example of cross-cutting perf: kernel selection + batching + keying all interact. Please keep experiment notes concise in the PRs so we can replay.
Liam W.: copying experiment logs to the perf-runbook: https://redwood/internal/perf/prefill/186700-canary
Anna K.: :thumbsup:
